title: io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension (SEP-2663, released 2026-07-28) - the pin ghantika's Tasks-extension adapter is checked against
description: Vendored, in-repo pin (never an npm dependency - no io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks package exists to depend on) of the RELEASED SEP-2663 contract itself, not our own emitted shape. Before story-0137 this file documented what src/tasksAdapter.ts happened to return; tasksAdapter.ts's own header discloses it was designed before finalization and never reconciled, so that earlier version pinned our own pre-finalization guess, not the spec. This version pins the spec's actual field names, discriminated status variants, and request/response shapes, measured directly against the spec's own generated schema.json (modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks) rather than summarized text; scripts/check-sdk-exact-pin.mjs's schema-vs-implementation check is what now verifies our adapter conforms TO this pin, rather than this pin describing the adapter. config/tasks-schema-digest.json records this file's SHA-256 so drift between the two is caught, not silently trusted. Every variant below restates its own fields in full rather than composing a shared base via `allOf` or `$ref`-plus-siblings: test/tasks.test.ts's hand-rolled validator implements only the keyword set this schema actually needs, `allOf` deliberately not among them (extending it is test-infrastructure work this repo has been directed to stop), and that same validator resolves a `$ref` by replacing the node it appears on, so a `$ref` next to sibling properties would silently validate nothing. The duplication below is the honest cost of staying inside that validator's real behavior. Every task-shaped variant locks `additionalProperties: false` to match the real spec exactly (measured: every DetailedTask variant, and the base Task type, locks it) - a pin that stayed looser than its own contract could never red on a shape the spec itself rejects. The spec's own DetailedTask union uses `anyOf`; this schema uses `oneOf` instead, deliberately - the four status consts are mutually exclusive by construction so the two are behaviorally identical here, and `oneOf` (unlike `anyOf`) is a keyword the validator above actually implements.

taskStatus.description: The spec's closed, five-value status enum. ghantika only ever EMITS four of these ('working', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled') - see emittedTaskStatus below for that narrower, honestly-reachable set. 'input_required' is a legal spec value this schema must accept (a conformant client cannot assume it never appears from a Tasks-capable server in general), but it is structurally unreachable from ghantika specifically: a job-backed task has no client-input step, so ghantika's own adapter never constructs an InputRequiredTask.

emittedTaskStatus.description: The subset of taskStatus ghantika's adapter actually produces. A deep-equals against the full taskStatus enum above is not a valid conformance check once this schema pins the spec's five values - test/tasks.test.ts asserts this set is a SUBSET of taskStatus.enum, not equal to it, and states why 'input_required' is excluded (structurally unreachable, not merely unobserved).

taskOutputCounts.description: The backing job's real, ever-cumulative output volume (never decremented by retention eviction). ghantika's own extension of the spec's free-form CompletedTask.result / FailedTask.error JSONObject, not a spec-defined field name itself.

watchStoppedInfo.description: Present once this adapter's own output-driven notification WATCH (the wake accelerator - see notifications/tasks/status) has auto-stopped early - currently only ever for a sustained firehose rate. Never means the backing job stopped. ghantika's own extension of the spec's free-form result/error JSONObject on a TERMINAL task. On a still-'working' task, the SAME fact (reason plus timestamp) is rendered as text into that variant's spec-legal, otherwise-unused `statusMessage` field instead - see workingTask below - since WorkingTask locks `additionalProperties: false` and has no free-form container of its own to carry this structured shape.

ghantikaResultExtras.description: ghantika's own additions inside the spec's free-form CompletedTask.result / FailedTask.error JSONObject - never top-level Task fields, since the spec's base Task/WorkingTask/CancelledTask interfaces carry no such container and a1 requires every top-level field we emit to be one the spec defines.

workingTask.description: The spec's WorkingTask: Task's base fields, status pinned to 'working', no result/error - restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's header. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec exactly (measured against modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks's generated schema.json).

statusMessage.description: Free text per the spec - optional, no format constraint. ghantika's ONE use of it: when this adapter's own output-driven notification watch has auto-stopped early (see watchStoppedInfo) while the task is still 'working', the same fact (the fixed 'firehose' reason plus a stoppedAt timestamp - a constant and a timestamp, nothing else) is rendered into this field as text, since a still-working task has no free-form container the way a terminal task's result/error does. This field is otherwise unused by ghantika today.

completedTask.description: The spec's CompletedTask: Task's base fields, status pinned to 'completed', plus the spec's free-form result JSONObject (ghantika's own exitCode/output/watchStopped live inside it, see ghantikaResultExtras) - restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's header. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec exactly.

failedTask.description: The spec's FailedTask: Task's base fields, status pinned to 'failed', plus the spec's free-form error JSONObject (ghantika's own exitCode/output/watchStopped live inside it, see ghantikaResultExtras) - restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's header. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec exactly.

cancelledTask.description: The spec's CancelledTask: Task's base fields, status pinned to 'cancelled', no result/error - restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's header. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec exactly.

detailedTask.description: The spec's DetailedTask discriminated union, narrowed to the four variants ghantika's job model can ever actually produce (working / completed / failed / cancelled - never input_required). A pure oneOf of bare $refs - no siblings alongside either $ref, which is the one form this repo's hand-rolled validator resolves correctly. The spec's own union uses anyOf; oneOf is used here deliberately, see this schema's top-level header.

createTaskResult.description: CreateTaskResult = Result & Task per the spec: the flat base-Task shape (never a DetailedTask variant - a freshly minted task carries no result/error yet even if the backing job happened to already be terminal at mint time), with resultType:'task' replacing the normal CallToolResult content/structuredContent shape. Returned by run() on a Tasks-capable connection - see this schema's header note on the still-unconfirmed wire mechanics of this replacement (resultType itself is SEP-2322/core-protocol vocabulary, not redefined in the tasks extension's own generated schema - the exact envelope needs pinning against the installed SDK's own types as a first build step, not this fetch). Restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's top-level header. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec's own Task-shaped branch of CreateTaskResult exactly.

getTaskResultWorking.description: GetTaskResult's 'working' branch: WorkingTask's fields plus resultType:'complete', restated in full - see getTaskResult below. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec exactly.

getTaskResultCompleted.description: GetTaskResult's 'completed' branch: CompletedTask's fields plus resultType:'complete', restated in full - see getTaskResult below. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec exactly.

getTaskResultFailed.description: GetTaskResult's 'failed' branch: FailedTask's fields plus resultType:'complete', restated in full - see getTaskResult below. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec exactly.

getTaskResultCancelled.description: GetTaskResult's 'cancelled' branch: CancelledTask's fields plus resultType:'complete', restated in full - see getTaskResult below. `additionalProperties: false`, matching the real spec exactly.

getTaskResult.description: GetTaskResult = Result & DetailedTask per the spec: resultType:'complete' flattened alongside whichever DetailedTask variant matches the task's current status. Returned by tasks/get (and, in ghantika's own design, also by tasks/update - see ackResult for the spec-defined tasks/update shape this schema does NOT use). A pure oneOf of bare $refs to the four resultType-carrying variants above, each already self-contained - never composed via allOf or $ref-plus-siblings, see this schema's top-level header. The spec's own composition uses anyOf; oneOf is used here deliberately, see this schema's top-level header.

ackResult.description: UpdateTaskResult / CancelTaskResult per the spec: an empty acknowledgement carrying only resultType:'complete', nothing else. Both are eventually-consistent per the spec - the ack may arrive before the task's observable status reflects the requested change. NOTE: the real spec's own UpdateTaskResult/CancelTaskResult leave additionalProperties permissive (measured: `{}`, not `false`); this schema pins `false` here, STRICTER than the released contract rather than looser - flagged, not changed without sign-off, since a stricter pin can only reject a shape the real spec would accept, never accept one the spec rejects (the opposite direction from the defect this schema's other additionalProperties locks exist to close).

taskNotFoundError.description: Not a success-result shape at all. The spec answers an unknown OR an expired-and-purged taskId with the same JSON-RPC error code (-32602, Invalid params) - it does not differentiate the two at the protocol level, so ghantika's prior tagged-success taskNotFound shape is retired: tasks/get, tasks/update, and tasks/cancel alike now THROW rather than returning a value shaped like this. Kept here only as documentation of the error code this schema's consumers must expect, not as a schema any response is validated against.
